claims.claim: Travers and Milgram reported 296 initiated chains, 64 completed chains, and a mean of 5.2 intermediaries among completed chains.
claims.notes: Mean applies only to completed chains; it is not a universal distance between all people.

claims.claim: Watts and Strogatz studied networks interpolating between regular and random topologies through random rewiring.
claims.locator: Nature 393 (1998), pp. 440–442; model construction and Fig. 1

claims.claim: For the regular ring lattice with even degree K, the local clustering coefficient is 3(K−2)/[4(K−1)].
claims.locator: Watts and Strogatz (1998), regular ring construction; count neighbor-neighbor edges

claims.claim: Short average path length does not by itself guarantee decentralized search; navigability depends on long-range link distribution.
claims.locator: Kleinberg (2000), The Small-World Phenomenon: An Algorithmic Perspective
